text:
Detroit comes in as the team that has controlled more of the play. At five on five, the Red Wings have taken 52% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality), against 45% for Seattle, and the model has them slightly ahead tonight, 3.26 to 2.85. Both teams give up plenty, but Seattle gives up more, 3.52 expected goals per 60 to Detroit's 3.28. On special teams, Detroit's power play (0.91 expected goals a game) outpaces Seattle's (0.54), though the Red Wings take 4.75 penalties a game, which keeps handing the other side chances.

Both teams are 2 days off their last games, and recent form is close. Detroit is 2-1-2 in its last five, Seattle 3-1-1, and Seattle's results have run ahead of its chances: a +3 goal difference on -5.2 expected. Finishing is doing the lifting. In net, projected starter Daniil Tarasov has saved 5.4 goals above expected this season, in just three games, but was at -2.84 last year over 33. Seattle's projected starter, Joey Daccord, is at -2.35 this season and -6.1 last. Seattle won the first meeting 6-3 on Oct 9, though by chances it deserved only 42% of that win.

For Detroit, Alex DeBrincat is one goal from 300 career goals and has a 42% chance to score tonight, the top mark on either roster. Lucas Raymond has gone without a goal in eight games despite 2.9 expected goals, so the chances are there. Seattle's Jared McCann tops the Kraken at 30%. Brandon Montour could return for Seattle after moving to day-to-day.
